doc.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sonny Rollins on the Five Spot trio
summary: Carter praises Rollins's long explorations of one tune in the six-to-eight-week trio engagement.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Again, anytime he'd call me, I'd be available. We worked together in New York at the old Five Spot for probably six, eight weeks with a trio: saxophone, bass and drums. Every night was like going to school because how he would manipulate the chords and how he would play the melody and how long he would play the tune to develop it, which he thought he could, for the space of time. Maybe a half hour of this tune and maybe twelve choruses of this tune, and maybe just a tune twice a night until he felt that he had kind of gotten all he could get out of it. He was respectful of bass players; he listened to bass all the time. Of course he had no piano. And I been promising myself I'd call him and just scare him by saying "hello" on the phone, but I haven't gotten the nerve yet. But I love hearing him play.
